title: Binary Exploitation Quick Reference
description: Three steps from stack overflow to libc and common protection bypasses
detail:
1. checksec to inspect protections: NX/PIE/RELRO/Canary
2. Stack overflow: find the offset (cyclic) → ret2win → ret2libc (leak puts/GOT → calculate base → system(/bin/sh))
3. Format string: %p to leak → %n to write (overwrite GOT/return address/fini_array)
4. Heap: fastbin attack/tcache poisoning/UAF/unsorted bin leak (match glibc version)
5. Canary: leak (format string/output residue); PIE: partial overwrite
6. one_gadget / ROPgadget / pwntools templates (debug locally with the same libc version)
7. No-output environments: ret2dlresolve / SROP / ORW chains
8. Environment pitfall: target libc differs from local → use patchelf + specify ld (a common failure point in past team exercises)
Binary exploitation is a small portion of penetration assessments; when present, it is often simple ret2win/backdoor functions.
